audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors repeated across seven fields. (a) 'Kassadin's Q silence is 0.6 seconds' — Riot's Null Sphere text describes no silence; it says the orb interrupts channels. (b) 'his passive shield' — Void Stone is magic damage REDUCTION plus unit-collision immunity; the shield is on Null Sphere (Q). The claim that Twilight Assault 'bypasses his passive if he stands in the blade's path' is invented and reverses the truth: Void Stone reduces exactly that magic damage.
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupting channels is the decisive interaction in this matchup and it was absent — it cancels Stand United, Shen's stated win condition, at 650 range on a 9s rank-1 cooldown. The mirror audit (kassadin__shen) already put this interaction on the opposing page, so both sides now state it.
audit.corrected: Silence claims replaced with the channel interrupt in spikes[2], late, whys[6], wants.you[0], early. Passive re-stated as Void Stone damage reduction in spikes[0], spikes[3], early. Stand United's vulnerability added to breakdown.cooldowns and wants.you[2]. Riftwalk cooldown corrected from '6-second' to 5s rank 1 falling to 2s at rank 3.

edits.after: Null Sphere (Q) interrupts channels, so it cancels Stand United mid-cast — hold R until he has spent it, then your global teleport and frontline presence keep deciding fights while he hunts isolated picks.

edits.before: Kassadin has no escape tool and his passive shield only blocks magic damage — your Q-empowered autos deal magic damage through the blade, bypassing his passive if he stands in its path, and he cannot answer your E-taunt before level 6.
edits.after: Kassadin has no escape before Riftwalk, so Shadow Dash lands whenever you want it. Void Stone reduces the magic damage on Twilight Assault, so favour Grasp and item damage over pure Q chip and just hold him in the taunt.

edits.before: His biggest pre-6 threat is a forced trade where your E whiffs — if Shadow Dash misses on a minion or he sidesteps it, he walks forward under his passive shield and lands two Q-empowered autos before you can reset the blade.
edits.after: His biggest pre-6 threat is a forced trade where your E whiffs — Shadow Dash is down 18s at rank 1, so if it clips a minion he walks in behind the Null Sphere shield and lands Nether Blade resets for free.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the softest level 1-3 laners in the game — his passive shield blocks magic damage but your Q-empowered autos deal magic damage only if he stands in the spirit blade's path, so walk the blade through him on every trade and his passive absorbs nothing. At level 1 step up with the blade positioned between you and him and chip with auto-blade-auto; he has no dash and no meaningful answer. At level 2 your E comes online and this becomes a genuine bully lane — Shadow Dash into him for the taunt, throw Q to pull the blade through his body, then stand in the W zone to block whatever auto he manages to get off. His Q silence lasts under a second and he has no mobility to escape the taunt, so the full pattern lands cleanly every time. Shove the wave hard to deny him XP and consider a level 3 all-in if he is low — he has no defensive tool that stops your taunt.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the softest level 1-3 laners in the game — Void Stone reduces the magic damage on Twilight Assault, so lean on Grasp and raw autos rather than expecting the blade alone to chunk him. At level 1 step up with the blade positioned between you and him and chip with auto-blade-auto; he has no dash and no meaningful answer. At level 2 your E comes online and this becomes a genuine bully lane — Shadow Dash into him for the taunt, throw Q to pull the blade through his body, then stand in the W zone to block whatever auto he manages to get off. Null Sphere (Q) interrupts channels, not your dash, and he has no mobility until 6, so the full pattern lands cleanly every time. Shove the wave hard to deny him XP and consider a level 3 all-in if he is low — he has no defensive tool that stops your taunt.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the steadiest part of this lane: Kassadin is farming defensively waiting for 6 and you should respect that he is building Force Pulse stacks from range. Do not overextend to chase; hold your Q-blade trade pattern and freeze or slow-push to keep him starved. At level 6 Riftwalk changes the lane geometry — he can now blink through your E on a 6-second cooldown, so forcing an all-in becomes riskier. This is exactly when you should stop trying to kill him and start treating Stand United as your primary win condition. Every shove top is a signal to check the minimap for a collapsing lane; a well-timed R teleport to a 2v1 fight is worth far more than trading a gank for a plate here. Keep him under tower pressure to deny his roam options — Kassadin top without Teleport is a dead roam threat, so tracking his summoner cooldowns matters.

edits.before: Full AP Kassadin is a serious late-game carry in teamfights — his Riftwalk stacks make him slippery and his burst can one-shot carries. However his Q silence lasts less than a second and his only peel tool is the blink itself, which means he cannot cleanly escape your W-block zone in a coordinated fight. Your job late is to be the frontline initiator who E-taunts the first target while your carries punish the backline chaos; if Kassadin blinks to your backline, your W will blank his auto-reset window and buy your team the reaction time. Keep Hollow Radiance fully stacked and stand in the most contested areas of every teamfight — your 52% win rate in this matchup is built on global R tempo and teamfight presence, not a lane stomp, so never stray far from your team in the late game.
edits.after: Full AP Kassadin is a serious late-game carry in teamfights — his Riftwalk stacks make him slippery and his burst can one-shot carries. His Null Sphere (Q) interrupts channels, so he can cancel Stand United out of the air: cast R from fog or only once you have seen him blink. edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3. Track it before every engage. - Null Sphere (Q), 9s: interrupts your Stand United channel. - Your ultimate: kill windows only, cast from fog.

notes: The 'Q silence 0.6s' number appears nowhere in Riot's Null Sphere text and I could not verify it from the kits, so I did not restate any silence duration — I replaced it with the interaction Riot does document, the channel interrupt. Void Stone was described as a shield in three fields; it is damage reduction, and the old text told the player his Twilight Assault bypassed it, which is backwards. Level 6 already read Skill in both layers; only Levels 4-5 needed the flip.
